Dielectric confinement (also called image charge effect) manifests in a quantum well system provided that the thickness of the quantum wells is comparable to the exciton size, and the dielectric constant ratio between the quantum wells (perovskite layers with ε w ~4 or higher) and the barriers (organic spacing layers with ε b ~2.2) is larger than unity. This result leads to an enhancement of the Coulomb interaction between the electron and hole pair composing each exciton, which is a consequence of the reduced dielectric screening of the exciton electric field partially located outside the quantum well, i.e., in the surrounding barriers that have a lower dielectric constant.
